audit_findings.title: Sold MEMS earnings may be capitalized while sale proceeds are also added as cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $878 million cash proceeds and $44 million earn-out fair value; MEMS owner earnings unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor retains earnings from the subsequently sold operation, while the June 2026 cash bridge reflects the post-sale balance sheet; projecting those earnings after the disposal duplicates value already realized through the sale.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 2, 2026, NXP completed the previously announced sale of our MEMS sensors business line for $900 million in cash before closing adjustments and up to an additional $50 million contingent upon the achievement of specified technical milestones.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filing does not disclose MEMS owner earnings or how much of the sale cash remained in the June balance after debt repayment and other uses. The direction is upward if sold earnings remain in projected OE, but the record cannot establish the valuation impact.
audit_findings.action: Build a continuing-perimeter FY2025 OE bridge excluding MEMS revenue, costs, working capital and maintenance capex; retain the actual June cash balance and separately include the filed $44 million earn-out receivable if it is absent from the bridge, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: VSMC imposes a large off-balance-sheet minimum-loading obligation absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $14,096 million nominal over 37 years, approximately $381 million per year by simple average; value impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The loading floor will enter future OE through wafer purchase costs, utilization losses, inventory and working-capital requirements, while usable capacity could also support growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, NXP has an agreed purchase commitment with VSMC that over the lifetime of the factory the minimal loading will be between 80 % - 90 %, resulting in a total purchase commitment of approximately $ 14,096 million that is expected to be purchased over 37 years once wafer production starts.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitment is filed and large relative to the $1,708 million OE anchor, but it begins after the anchor and purchases should produce saleable wafers. There is no demonstrated loss unless contracted capacity exceeds economically usable demand or pricing is unfavorable, so the gross commitment must not be deducted as a liability.
audit_findings.action: Obtain production-start timing, contracted wafer pricing, annual capacity, cancellation or resale rights and downside demand assumptions; model only incremental cost or underutilization losses against the value of usable output.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor is not a full-year measure of the acquired perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,160 million aggregate net cash consideration; each acquired business contributed less than 1% of FY2025 revenue; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Partial-year acquisition results enter the OE anchor, while the valuation-date perimeter contains the acquired businesses for a full year; financing, integration costs and continuing operating contributions may also be mismatched.
audit_findings.evidence: Management's assessment of the effectiveness of the Company's internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, excluded TTTech Auto, Aviva and Kinara, each of which were acquired during the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but revenue scale does not establish earnings scale. Full-year contributions could increase OE if the businesses are profitable or reduce it if they remain loss-making or require substantial integration spending, so materiality and direction cannot be determined from the record.
audit_findings.action: Prepare twelve-month pro forma OE for TTTech Auto, Aviva Links and Kinara, including cash operating costs, integration costs, maintenance investment and incremental interest expense, and combine it with the MEMS-excluded continuing perimeter before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Separately added stakes may overlap with equity-accounted results retained in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,305 million stakes bridge; FY2025 equity-accounted loss of $70 million, comprising $8 million share of losses and $62 million of other results
audit_findings.mechanism: Investee income, losses and impairments can remain in OE while the underlying investments are separately added through the equity bridge, causing inconsistent capitalization between OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Results relating to equity-accounted investees amounted to a loss of $70 million in 2025, whereas in 2024 results relating to equity-accounted investees amounted to a loss of $12 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $1,305 million bridge equals the filed June 2026 carrying value of equity investments, but the record does not establish whether the $70 million FY2025 loss was removed from calculated OE or which loss components correspond to investments still owned. Retaining recurring losses tends to understate value, while adding stakes without recognizing future losses or funding needs can overstate it.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every dollar of stakes_net to the June 2026 investment schedule; identify which investee results entered the $1,708 million anchor, remove all income, losses and one-time impairments associated with separately valued stakes, and model required future funding before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: Time-limited government assistance may have been treated as perpetual earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $185 million FY2025 operating assistance, including $83 million of R&D tax credits and $102 million of direct grants; expiring IPCEI portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Government assistance reduces operating expenditures included in OE; perpetuating the portion scheduled to expire in 2029 inflates forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our direct grants include those awarded under the European 2nd Important Project of Common European Interest on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies (“IPCEI ME/CT”) in multiple EU member states, the duration of which is planned to run until the end of 2029.
audit_findings.explanation: A temporary grant stream is demonstrated, but the filing does not disclose how much of the $102 million of direct grants came from IPCEI or whether qualifying expenditure will fall, replacement support will arise, or repayment conditions will be triggered. The affected amount may be meaningful relative to the $1,708 million anchor, but materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 IPCEI benefit by program and expense line, associated incremental expenditures and repayment conditions; run the grants off through 2029 and exclude them from terminal OE unless replacement funding is evidenced.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash is not wholly attributable to common shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $139.3 million maximum adjustment, equal to 38.8% of $359 million SSMC cash; approximately $0.54 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The cash bridge adds consolidated SSMC cash at 100%, although 38.8% of distributions belongs to the non-controlling joint-venture partner.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the terms of our joint venture agreement with TSMC, a portion of this cash can be distributed by way of a dividend to us, but 38.8% of the dividend will be paid to our joint venture partner.
audit_findings.explanation: The attribution error is demonstrated. Even treating all $359 million of SSMC cash as distributable, the common-shareholder overstatement is at most $139.3 million, only 0.51% of the $27,232 million base equity value and about $0.54 versus base value of $105.75 per share. It cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reduce bridge cash by TSMC's 38.8% share of distributable SSMC cash and separately determine any operating-cash reserve; no full scenario redesign is required.
